not_for_investment_decision: No validated forecast, confidence score, host attestation, or skill publication is claimed.

common_scenario_conditions.low: Slower AI consumption and paid adoption, delayed capacity, weaker enterprise budgets, persistent device inventory and failed gaming recovery.
common_scenario_conditions.base: Delivered cloud growth and paid AI mix coexist with on-premise migration and device correction; no material new acquisition/FX benefit assumed.
common_scenario_conditions.high: Supply and customer consumption expand together, paid AI retention is robust, enterprise adoption widens, and legacy/consumer stabilization is faster.
common_scenario_conditions.probabilities: None; conditional scenarios are not calibrated prediction intervals.

curves.name: Azure
curves.rationale: New-perimeter FY26 growth was about 40%; FY27 Q1 outlook 44-45% CC. Base allows a strong first half then moderation; low represents delayed energization/consumption and high sustained delivery. Later-year decay is analyst judgment, not management guidance or estimated probability.
curves.data_gap: Billable compute/token consumption and realized revenue per unit are unavailable; capex is not revenue-capable capacity. No independent capacity ceiling is quantified.
curves.falsifier: Two successive quarters of comparable Azure growth below 30%, reduced consumption or material commissioning delays would challenge Base.

curves.name: Microsoft 365 cloud
curves.rationale: New-perimeter FY26 cloud growth is observed; FY27 Q1 commercial CC guide roughly 17% and consumer mid-teens. Base reflects seat growth plus premium mix/AI monetization then gradual maturation; low represents weak paid retention and mix dilution; high requires renewed paid expansion. Published guide is not identical to aggregate GAAP cloud revenue.
curves.data_gap: No same-perimeter average paid seats, realized net ARPU or opening/closing ARR bridge. Paid end-period GitHub/365 seats and list prices cannot reconstruct recognized annual revenue.
leading_indicators: paid seat growth on recast basis
curves.falsifier: Comparable seat growth below 4% or commercial-cloud growth below 12% for two quarters undermines Base.

curves.name: Productivity and server licensing
curves.rationale: FY27 Q1 recast guide low-single decline and FY27 original product/server guide mid-single decline support shrinkage. Base treats cloud migration as persistent but moderating; low adds accelerated substitution; high is stable recognition. Migration must not be added again to cloud growth.
curves.data_gap: Cloud migration cohort, licensing renewal calendar, standalone selling prices and contract recognition mix unavailable.
curves.falsifier: Licensing grows persistently while cloud growth does not weaken, or decline exceeds 10%, requiring re-evaluation of mix and recognition.

curves.name: Search and advertising
curves.rationale: FY27 Q1 ex-TAC outlook is mid-to-high single growth; Base takes a moderate GAAP path with stable TAC/mix only as an assumption. Low reflects weaker ad demand and monetization; high requires share plus pricing gains. GAAP and ex-TAC growth are not treated as identical facts.
curves.data_gap: Missing eligible impressions, realized CPM, TAC bridge and LinkedIn premium-subscription carve-out; forecast remains a mixed stream fallback.
curves.falsifier: ex-TAC growth falls below 3% or TAC/mix reverses so that GAAP growth diverges materially from Base.

curves.name: XBOX
curves.rationale: Recent revenue decline and weak FY27 Q1 contrast with management's return-to-growth aim. Base makes only a slight first-year recovery then modest content-led growth; low explicitly allows target failure; high requires successful releases and subscriptions. No probability assigned.
curves.data_gap: No independently verified title-by-title release timing, paid cohorts, payer monetization or hardware/content mix bridge.
curves.falsifier: A material content delay or another full-year decline invalidates the near-term recovery mechanism.

curves.name: Industry solutions
curves.rationale: Recast cloud outlook high-single growth plus mixed products supports a cautious growth path; Base allows ERP and industry adoption with CRM hiring-cycle drag. Low assumes sales cycles remain elongated; high requires broad customer conversion.
curves.data_gap: Dynamics/LinkedIn/Healthcare units and pricing are not separately reconciled under new perimeter. Industry cloud KPI is not the whole mixed revenue line.
curves.falsifier: Cloud growth below 5% for two quarters or delayed customer projects challenges Base.

curves.name: Windows OEM and devices
curves.rationale: FY27 outlook high-teens decline and Q1 low-twenties decline inform a weak first year. Base assumes inventory normalization followed by small replacement recovery; low prolongs component-cost and demand stress; high assumes faster normalization. No fabricated unit shipments.
curves.data_gap: No same-perimeter OEM license units, hardware unit mix, realized pricing or channel stock-flow history.
curves.falsifier: Persistent excess inventory or a further double-digit decline in FY28 invalidates Base normalization.

curves.name: Frontier and support services
curves.rationale: Service attachment to deployed enterprise systems supports moderate growth near its recent range. Low reflects customer budget rationalization; high assumes deployment and support demand. This is analyst extrapolation, with no exact management full-year target.
curves.data_gap: No billable hours, realized fee rates, headcount utilization or contracted-service backlog bridge.
curves.falsifier: Services decline despite cloud deployment growth suggests decoupling and invalidates the attach assumption.

formal_blockers: Capture-ready canonical 10-K required for recognition review
Actual source_preparation record and immutable source capture required
Material guidance ledger and checked evidence claims not yet built
Long-horizon assumptions lack frozen out-of-sample calibration
Underlying unit/price data insufficient for auditable operating identities

historical_arithmetic_checks.result_scope: Historical arithmetic only; no revenue_forecast.py run or publication receipt
